name: MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark
description: MVBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). It covers 20 challenging video tasks that cannot be effectively solved with a single frame, ranging from action recognition to counterfactual inference. The benchmark uses a static-to-dynamic method to systematically define temporal-related tasks by adapting static image tasks with dynamic evolution.

citeAs: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao. MVBench: A Comprehensive Multi-modal Video Understanding Benchmark. arXiv:2311.17005v4 [cs.CV] 23 May 2024
rai:dataCollection: MVBench data is collected from 11 public video datasets including STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. Videos are carefully filtered based on temporal sensitivity (intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s), video diversity (covering first-person to third-person perspectives, indoor to outdoor environments), and question difficulty. The benchmark produces 200 multiple-choice QA pairs for each of the 20 temporal understanding tasks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos are sourced from 11 existing public video benchmarks: STAR (real-world indoor third-person), PAXION (real-world and simulated indoor/outdoor third-person), Moments in Time V1 (real-world and simulated indoor/outdoor third-person), FunQA (real-world indoor/outdoor third-person), CLEVRER (simulated indoor), Perception Test (real-world indoor first and third-person), Charades-STA (real-world indoor third-person), MoVQA (real-world indoor/outdoor third-person), NTU RGB+D (real-world indoor third-person), VLN-CE (simulated indoor first-person), and TVQA (real-world indoor/outdoor third-person).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For STAR dataset, the challenge was enhanced by randomly shifting the start or end points of video clips to increase the complexity of localizing specific events. For CLEVRER, questions requiring more than 10 conditions for describing specific events were excluded to decrease QA difficulty. Videos with intermediate duration (primarily 5s to 35s) were selected, eliminating short clips with minimal movement and extremely long videos with overly complicated contexts.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data filtration was performed based on three criteria: (1) Video Diversity: selecting 11 video datasets covering broad spectrum of domains and scenes; (2) Temporal Sensitivity: eliminating short clips and extremely long videos, selecting videos with intermediate duration primarily ranging from 5s to 35s; (3) Question Difficulty: balancing difficulty by applying specific selection criteria for STAR and CLEVRER datasets. Videos are processed using TSN sampling, with 4-frame videos in Stage1 and Stage2, 8-frame videos in Stage3, and 16-frame videos for evaluation at 224×224 resolution.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multiple-choice QAs are automatically generated from public video annotations using two methods: (1) Template-Based Construction: option candidates are constructed directly from ground truth annotations (e.g., for Action Antonym task, candidates contain correct action, its opposite action, and a not-sure choice); (2) LLM-Based Generation: ChatGPT is used to generate questions based on task definitions and to convert open-ended QAs into multiple-choice format with answer options. For all questions, 3 to 5 answer options are randomly sampled from available candidates, and option order is shuffled. LLM is used to ensure all answer options have similar and reasonable lengths to prevent answer leakage.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer options are randomly selected and shuffled to strengthen evaluation robustness. All answer options of a question are ensured to be of similar and reasonable lengths using LLM to prevent the common issue of answer leakage where longer options tend to be correct. A detailed system prompt encourages MLLMs to carefully scrutinize video content, and an answer prompt 'Best Option: (' is used to guide MLLMs for option generation, achieving 100% rate in option extraction.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 200 multiple-choice QA pairs for each of the 20 temporal understanding tasks
rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT for question generation and QA conversion; UMT-L/16 for action predictions in Fine-grained Action task
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that there is a minimal source gap between instruction data and MVBench. Specifically, CLEVRER in instruction data has similar questions as Moving Attribute and Counterfactual Inference in MVBench, and videos of Action Antonym are from SthSthV2 while the antonym is from PAXION. Results show more pronounced influence from CLEVRER data while SthSthV2 data appears to have less effect.
rai:dataLimitations: Current MLLMs have difficulty generalizing to localization and counting tasks in the absence of related tuning data. For position-related tasks, none of the models achieve satisfactory results, with performances analogous to random guessing. For counting and character-related tasks, VideoChat2 performs similarly and even worse than VideoChat2_text without videos. In cognition tasks, VideoChat2 encounters difficulties with complex egocentric navigation and episode reasoning. The paper suggests that visual information alone may not be sufficient and inclusion of other modalities such as depth and audio could prove beneficial.
rai:dataUseCases: MVBench is designed for evaluating the temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs). The benchmark is used for testing and validation of MLLMs across 20 temporal understanding tasks including action sequence, action prediction, action antonym, fine-grained action, unexpected action, object existence, object interaction, object shuffle, moving direction, action localization, scene transition, action count, moving count, moving attribute, state change, fine-grained pose, character order, egocentric navigation, episodic reasoning, and counterfactual inference. The evaluation uses multiple-choice QA format with accuracy as the metric.
